meta.titre: Velocity-time graphs: gradient, area and multi-stage journeys

sections.contenu_markdown: A minibus leaves the bus park in Bamenda, speeds up on the straight road, cruises for a while and finally slows to a stop at the next town. If a passenger records the speed every few seconds, the numbers can be drawn as a velocity-time graph, and that single picture tells the whole journey: how quickly the bus gained speed, how long it cruised and how far it went. Almost every GCE paper contains a velocity-time question with a table of readings or a sketch, so it pays to read the gradient and the area with confidence.

items: Velocity is the distance moved per second in a stated direction and is measured in metres per second ($\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$).
Acceleration is the change of velocity per second, measured in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
The area of a rectangle is base times height, of a triangle is half base times height, of a trapezium is half the sum of the parallel sides times the height.

sections.titre: Gradient, area and the shape of a velocity-time graph
sections.contenu_markdown:
On a **velocity-time graph**, time $t$ is on the horizontal axis and velocity $v$ on the vertical axis.

**Gradient = acceleration.**

$$a=\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}=\frac{v_2-v_1}{t_2-t_1}\quad(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$$

**Area under the graph = distance travelled** (displacement for motion in a straight line).

**Reading the shape:**

| Part of the graph | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Straight line sloping up | constant (uniform) acceleration |
| Horizontal straight line | constant velocity, acceleration $=0$ |
| Straight line sloping down | uniform deceleration (negative acceleration) |
| Line along the time axis ($v=0$) | the object is at rest |
| Curved line | changing acceleration |

**Areas to use:** rectangle $=v\times t$; triangle $=\tfrac12\times t\times v$; trapezium $=\tfrac12(v_1+v_2)\,t$. For several stages, calculate each area separately and add.

**Average speed** $=\dfrac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}$, using the **total** area under the graph.

**Data in a table.** When the graph is given as pairs of $(t,v)$ values, treat each pair of consecutive readings as the ends of a straight segment. For each segment find the acceleration $\Delta v/\Delta t$ and the distance using the trapezium area $\tfrac12(v_1+v_2)\Delta t$. If the acceleration is the same in consecutive segments, they lie on one straight line.

variantes.nom: Plotting a graph from a table of readings
variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must draw the graph before reading values from it.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Put time on the horizontal axis and velocity on the vertical axis, label both with units, choose a scale that uses more than half the page, plot each point with a small cross and draw a smooth line through them (a straight ruler line where the points lie on a straight line). To find an acceleration, draw a **large** gradient triangle on the line, read its vertical and horizontal sides from the axes and divide: $a=\dfrac{\text{vertical side}}{\text{horizontal side}}$.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the acceleration is uniform and you need v, a, t or s without drawing.
variantes.contenu_markdown: For a straight-line segment from initial velocity $u$ to final velocity $v$ in time $t$: the gradient gives $a=\dfrac{v-u}{t}$, i.e. $v=u+at$; the trapezium area gives the distance $s=\tfrac12(u+v)\,t$.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A bus is observed on a straight road. Its velocity is recorded as follows, and between consecutive readings the velocity changes uniformly.

| Time $t$ / $\mathrm{s}$ | 0 | 6 | 16 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Velocity $v$ / $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ | 0 | 12 | 12 | 0 |

(a) Calculate the acceleration in each of the three stages.

(b) Calculate the total distance travelled.

(c) Calculate the average speed for the whole journey.

etapes.action: Split the motion into three straight stages.
etapes.justification: A straight line segment joins each pair of consecutive readings.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Stage 1: $0$ to $6\ \mathrm{s}$; stage 2: $6$ to $16\ \mathrm{s}$; stage 3: $16$ to $20\ \mathrm{s}$.

etapes.action: Find each acceleration from the gradient.
Find the distance in each stage from the area.
etapes.justification: Triangle in stages 1 and 3, rectangle in stage 2.
The total area under the graph is the total distance.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $0$ and $-3\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ (the bus slows down in stage 3). **(b)** $180\ \mathrm{m}$. **(c)** **$9\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**.

items.erreur_markdown: “A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph means the object is stationary.”
items.pourquoi_faux: A horizontal line means the velocity is constant and not zero. That is the rule for a distance-time graph. The object is at rest only when the line lies on the time axis.
items.correction_markdown: Horizontal line: constant velocity, zero acceleration. Line at $v=0$: at rest.

items.pourquoi_faux: That is the area of a rectangle. A triangle under a straight line from the origin has half that area.

items.erreur_markdown: “The graph slopes downwards, so the object is moving backwards.”
items.pourquoi_faux: The velocity is still positive, so the object still moves forwards, only more slowly. A downward slope means a negative acceleration (deceleration).
items.correction_markdown: The object moves backwards only if the line goes below the time axis.

items.erreur_markdown: Acceleration of a journey that starts at $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ taken as $\dfrac{v}{t}=\dfrac{14}{5}$
items.pourquoi_faux: Acceleration is the change in velocity. The initial velocity is not zero, so it must be subtracted.

items.erreur_markdown: Finding the total distance by multiplying the final velocity by the total time.
items.pourquoi_faux: The velocity changes during the journey, so that product is not the area under the graph.
items.correction_markdown: Add the areas of the separate stages (triangles, rectangles, trapezia).

items.enonce_markdown:
A motorcycle accelerates uniformly from rest to $15\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in $5.0\ \mathrm{s}$.

(a) Calculate its acceleration.

(b) Calculate the distance it travels in this time.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $a=\dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{15-0}{5.0}=$ **$3.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$**.

(b) Distance = area of the triangle $=\tfrac12\times5.0\times15=$ **$37.5\ \mathrm{m}$**.

items.enonce_markdown:
The velocity of a car is recorded as follows (uniform change between readings).

| Time $t$ / $\mathrm{s}$ | 0 | 5 | 15 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Velocity $v$ / $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ | 4 | 14 | 14 | 0 |

(a) Calculate the acceleration during the first $5\ \mathrm{s}$ and the deceleration during the last $5\ \mathrm{s}$.

(b) Calculate the total distance travelled.

(c) Calculate the average speed over the $20\ \mathrm{s}$.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) First stage: $a=\dfrac{14-4}{5}=$ **$2.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$**. Last stage: $a=\dfrac{0-14}{5}=-2.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, i.e. a deceleration of **$2.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$**.

(b) Stage 1 is a trapezium: $\tfrac12(4+14)\times5=45\ \mathrm{m}$. Stage 2 is a rectangle: $14\times10=140\ \mathrm{m}$. Stage 3 is a triangle: $\tfrac12\times5\times14=35\ \mathrm{m}$. Total $=45+140+35=$ **$220\ \mathrm{m}$**.

(c) Average speed $=\dfrac{220}{20}=$ **$11\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A bus leaves a stop and accelerates uniformly from rest at $1.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ for $10\ \mathrm{s}$. It then travels at constant velocity for a time $T$ and finally brakes uniformly at $3.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ until it stops. The total distance travelled is $450\ \mathrm{m}$.

(a) Calculate the maximum velocity.

(b) Calculate the distance covered while accelerating and the time and distance while braking.

(c) Calculate $T$.

(d) Calculate the average speed for the whole journey.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $v=u+at=0+1.5\times10=$ **$15\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**.

(b) Accelerating: distance $=\tfrac12\times10\times15=$ **$75\ \mathrm{m}$**. Braking: time $=\dfrac{15}{3.0}=$ **$5.0\ \mathrm{s}$**; distance $=\tfrac12\times5.0\times15=$ **$37.5\ \mathrm{m}$**.

(c) Distance at constant velocity $=450-75-37.5=337.5\ \mathrm{m}$, so $T=\dfrac{337.5}{15}=$ **$22.5\ \mathrm{s}$**.

(d) Total time $=10+22.5+5.0=37.5\ \mathrm{s}$. Average speed $=\dfrac{450}{37.5}=$ **$12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**.

items_markdown: Gradient of a velocity-time graph = acceleration: $a=\dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ (unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$).
Area under a velocity-time graph = distance travelled; use triangles, rectangles and trapezia and add the stages.
Horizontal line: constant velocity. Line sloping down: deceleration. Line on the time axis: at rest.
Average speed $=\dfrac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}$, not the average of the highest and lowest velocities unless the motion is uniform.
From a table, treat each pair of consecutive readings as a straight segment and calculate its acceleration and area separately.
